Build the gateway image locally, then deploy it by replacing the container

READ FIRST

How this assignment works

  • Share your screen in your breakout room, so we can drop in where it's useful.
  • exercises/lab.md is the source of truth; these slides summarise it. When they differ, follow lab.md.
  • You build, tag and deploy on your laptop. No registry today.
  • Your code takes the GitHub flow route: branch, PR on your fork, merge on GitHub, git pull.
  • Pre-flight: Docker with Compose v2 and ~8 GB free RAM.
Ask earlyStuck for more than a couple of minutes? Say so in the room. docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md covers the common stack, build and deploy failures.
THE PLAN

Three stops, in order

  1. TogetherBuild and inspect the image
  2. Part 1Change what goes into the image
  3. Part 2Deploy by replacing the container
SETUP

Go to this lab's folder and bring the stack up

  1. Get the latest course version (from any folder of your clone): it replaces your main, here and on your fork, so no merge conflicts.
  2. Stop the previous lab's stack (docker compose down in its folder) and go to this lab's folder in your course clone.
  3. Bring the stack up: setup.sh creates .env and starts local (:8088, bind-mounted), test (:8089) and production (:8090), plus TimescaleDB. Test and production stay empty until their first image deploy.
# 1: latest course version on main, here and on your fork
#    (replaces your main: no merge conflicts)
git fetch https://github.com/Mustry-Academy/cicd-for-ignition.git main \
  && git checkout -f -B main FETCH_HEAD && git push -f origin main

# 2: this lab's folder, previous stack down
cd ~/mustry-academy/cicd-for-ignition/labs/05-ignition-image-based-deploy
(cd ../04-ignition-file-based-deploy && docker compose down)

# 3: open VS Code, then bring the stack up
code .
scripts/setup.sh          # 3 gateways + TimescaleDB
Push rejected by a rule violation?Lab 03's protect-main ruleset is still on your fork: Settings › Rules › Rulesets › protect-main › Delete ruleset, then run step 1 again.
WE-DO · 1

Build the image, trace it to its commit, prove the cache

  1. scripts/build-image.sh builds the image and tags it :local. docker history shows the layers, newest on top: which is the biggest?
  2. Read the revision label back: it matches your last commit.
  3. touch a project file and rebuild: every layer stays CACHED. Append a newline and rebuild: only projects/ rebuilds.
  4. Drop a dummy file into third-party-modules/ and rebuild: the 5-second check, modules, config and projects all rebuild.
  5. Clean up: remove the dummy file, restore projects/ and rebuild.
# 1: build, then read the layers
scripts/build-image.sh
docker history cicd-lab-05-ignition:local

# 2: which commit was the image built from?
docker inspect -f '{{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision" }}' \
  cicd-lab-05-ignition:local
git rev-parse --short HEAD

# 3: touch only changes the date: every layer stays CACHED
touch projects/example-project/project.json
scripts/build-image.sh
#    a real edit: the projects/ layer rebuilds
printf '\n' >> projects/example-project/project.json
scripts/build-image.sh

# 4: a change in an earlier layer: every layer after it rebuilds
echo test > third-party-modules/dummy.txt
scripts/build-image.sh

# 5: clean up and rebuild
rm third-party-modules/dummy.txt && git checkout -- projects/ && \
  scripts/build-image.sh
WE-DO · 2

Run the image on its own and look at the files inside it

  1. Run the image on a spare port with no bind mounts: build-image.sh printed the same command.
  2. Follow the boot with docker logs -f demo. When the log shows "Starting project: example-project", wait a few seconds, then open http://localhost:9088: example-project is there, with no ./projects mount and no scan call. Ctrl-C only leaves the logs.
  3. Read the image, not the repo. In Docker Desktop (Images, cicd-lab-05-ignition, Files) or with --entrypoint find: projects/, config/ and modules.json under /usr/local/bin/ignition/data/, plus /third-party-modules. Not there: README.md, docs/, .env.
  4. Stop the demo gateway: --rm removes it.
# 1: the self-contained proof (-d = detached)
docker run -d --rm --name demo -p 9088:8088 \
  -e ACCEPT_IGNITION_EULA=Y \
  -e IGNITION_EDITION=standard \
  -e GATEWAY_ADMIN_USERNAME=admin \
  -e GATEWAY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=password \
  cicd-lab-05-ignition:local \
  -n demo -- -Dignition.allowunsignedmodules=true \
  -Dignition.gateway.externalModulesFolder=/third-party-modules

# 2: follow the boot (Ctrl-C leaves the logs)
docker logs -f demo

# 3: read the image itself
docker run --rm --entrypoint find cicd-lab-05-ignition:local \
  /usr/local/bin/ignition/data/projects -maxdepth 2

# 4: done exploring
docker stop demo

Part 1, solo: change what goes into the image, and prove it from the image

First: a branch off an up-to-date main
git switch main && git pull
git switch -c feature/image-change
  1. Part 1.1 · 10 minPut a config change in the image: a note on the gateway's Home page
  2. Part 1.2 · 10 minKeep a project export out with .dockerignore, merge, build v1.2
PART 1.1

Put a config change into the image and read it back

  1. Open services/config/resources/core/ignition/system-properties/config.json and replace the text of "homepageNotes" with a note of your own: a logged-in user sees it on the gateway's Home page.
  2. Rebuild. Which layers rebuilt, and which stayed CACHED? Why did the projects/ layer rebuild although you never touched a project?
  3. Prove it is in the image, not just in your folder: swap the entrypoint for grep and read the file inside the image.
# 1: edit the note
"homepageNotes": "Built into the gateway image. Deployed by replacing the container.",

# 2: rebuild
scripts/build-image.sh

# 3: read it back from the image
docker run --rm --entrypoint grep cicd-lab-05-ignition:local homepageNotes \
  /usr/local/bin/ignition/data/config/resources/core/ignition/system-properties/config.json
PART 1.2

Keep a project export out of the image with .dockerignore

  1. Someone saved a project export in projects/. Simulate it, rebuild, and find it in the image: it's there.
  2. Add **/*.zip to .dockerignore with a one-line comment. Rebuild, same find: gone from the image, still on your disk.
  3. Delete the file; git status shows only your two edits. Commit and push, then open the PR on GitHub, merge once lab05-ci.yml is green, and pull main.
  4. Build version v1.2 from main: the image Part 2 deploys.
# 1: a project export left in projects/
echo "pretend this is a project export" > projects/example-project-export.zip
scripts/build-image.sh
docker run --rm --entrypoint find cicd-lab-05-ignition:local \
  /usr/local/bin/ignition/data/projects -maxdepth 1

# 2: in .dockerignore, then rebuild + find again
# Project exports are copies of a project: keep them out of the image
**/*.zip

# 3: clean up, commit, push
rm projects/example-project-export.zip
git add .dockerignore services/config/resources/core/ignition/system-properties/config.json
git commit -m "Add a homepage note and keep project exports out of the image"
git push -u origin feature/image-change
#    on GitHub: open the PR, wait for green, merge
git switch main && git pull

# 4: build version v1.2
scripts/build-image.sh --tag v1.2

Part 2, solo: deploy your image to the test gateway by replacing the container

  1. Part 2.1 · 10 minDeploy v1.2 to test
  2. Part 2.2 · 15 minChange a view, build v1.3, deploy it
  3. Part 2.3 · 10 minRoll back to v1.2, check what survived

No registry involved: your local image store plays that role today.

PART 2.1

Deploy version v1.2 to the test gateway

  1. docker images lists v1.2 among the other tags.
  2. Before: which image does test run? The base image: an empty gateway. The historian's database: Did not find any relations.
  3. Deploy v1.2. Poll /StatusPing until it prints {"state":"RUNNING"}; RUNNING with COMMISSIONING is not done yet. Give it a few minutes.
  4. Verify: test now runs cicd-lab-05-ignition:v1.2. Launch example-project from :8089/app/home/perspective/session-launcher; log in at :8089: the Home page shows your Part 1.1 note.
  5. Run the psql line again: the historian's tables are there now.
# 1: your version
docker images cicd-lab-05-ignition

# 2: before: which image? and the DB
docker compose ps ignition-test
docker exec lab05-timescaledb psql -U ignition -d ignition_test -c '\dt'

# 3: THE deploy, then wait for RUNNING
IGNITION_TEST_IMAGE=cicd-lab-05-ignition:v1.2 \
  docker compose up -d ignition-test
curl -s localhost:8089/StatusPing   # repeat

# 4 + 5: run the ps and psql lines again
PART 2.2

Change a view, build v1.3 and deploy it

  1. Make a branch off an up-to-date main.
  2. Change the view in the Designer on the local gateway (:8088): open Perspective › Views › pages › overview, change the text of the Title label, File › Save All.
  3. Commit and push, then open the PR on GitHub, merge once it is green, and pull main.
  4. Build v1.3 and deploy it with the Part 2.1 command.
  5. Verify at :8089: your title is live and test runs v1.3. docker images shows v1.2 and v1.3: two versions, both on your machine.
# 1: a branch
git switch main && git pull
git switch -c feature/tweak-view
# 2: now change the Title in the Designer and save

# 3: commit and push
git status                     # only your view shows up
git add projects/ && git commit -m "Change overview title"
git push -u origin feature/tweak-view
#    on GitHub: open the PR, wait for green, merge
git switch main && git pull

# 4: build v1.3 and deploy it
scripts/build-image.sh --tag v1.3
IGNITION_TEST_IMAGE=cicd-lab-05-ignition:v1.3 \
  docker compose up -d ignition-test
PART 2.3

Roll back by running v1.2 again

  1. Pretend v1.3 broke something on test. You need the previous version back, now.
  2. Deploy v1.2: the same command, the older version. The old image never went away; it's a name in your image store.
  3. Verify at :8089: the title is back to its previous text, and test runs v1.2.
  4. Count the irreversible steps you just took. (Zero: both versions still exist, and you can flip between them as often as you like.)
# 2: rollback = the same deploy, the older version
IGNITION_TEST_IMAGE=cicd-lab-05-ignition:v1.2 \
  docker compose up -d ignition-test

# 3: which version runs on test now?
docker compose ps ignition-test
DONE?

Definition of done for Parts 1 and 2

Part 1
  • Your homepage note is in the image (--entrypoint grep); the project export is not (find before and after).
  • You built v1.2 from main after your PR was merged.
Part 2
  • The test gateway (:8089) runs your image, shown by docker compose ps.
  • You shipped a view change as v1.3: Designer, PR, build, deploy, visible on test.
  • Your image store holds v1.2 and v1.3, and you rolled test back to v1.2.
  • The historian's tables appeared with the first deploy and survived the later ones (psql … -c '\dt').
Debrief · 10 min
  • File-based vs image-based, having run both: which for your plant?
  • The rollback took one command: what made it that cheap?
  • Each deploy was a fresh gateway. Which state at your plant could not survive that, and where would you move it?
  • Put a registry in the middle (push + pull): what changes, and what stays exactly the same?
STRETCH

Let GitHub build the image, then deploy it by hand

  1. Only if the pull in step 2 says denied: log Docker in with a read:packages token, or make the package public.
  2. Your merges already built it: each one ran lab05-deploy.yml, which pushed that commit to your GHCR. Wait until the run for your Part 2.2 merge (the newest) is green.
  3. Deploy it yourself: the run's summary page prints the image name. Pull it and point test at it: the Part 2 command, longer name.
  4. Release: tag the latest main. lab05-release.yml checks :test was built from that commit, then re-tags it :v0.1.0 + :production: no rebuild. Deploy it to :8090.
  5. Compare the bytes: {{.Image}} is identical on test and production.
# 0: only if a pull says denied: log Docker in
gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages
gh auth token | docker login ghcr.io -u <your-user> --password-stdin

# 1: the newest deploy run is your Part 2.2 merge
gh run list --workflow lab05-deploy.yml --limit 3

# 2: copy the tag from the run summary, deploy it
docker pull ghcr.io/<your-user>/cicd-lab-05-ignition:sha-<short>
IGNITION_TEST_IMAGE=ghcr.io/<your-user>/cicd-lab-05-ignition:sha-<short> \
  docker compose up -d ignition-test

# 3: release (checked + promoted, no rebuild), deploy to :8090
git switch main && git pull
git tag lab05-v0.1.0 && git push origin lab05-v0.1.0
IGNITION_PRODUCTION_IMAGE=ghcr.io/<your-user>/cicd-lab-05-ignition:v0.1.0 \
  docker compose up -d ignition-production

# 4: compare the image bytes
docker inspect -f '{{.Image}}' lab05-ignition-test
docker inspect -f '{{.Image}}' lab05-ignition-production

You built the gateway as an image and deployed it by replacing the container

  • You put project, config and modules into a versioned image and proved it self-contained: no mounts, no scan.
  • You shipped a change end-to-end by hand: edit, commit, build, tag, recreate the container. That loop is what a pipeline automates.
  • You rolled test back by running the previous build's tag, and saw why versioned artifacts make that cheap.
  • Bring one surprise and one question to the debrief: file-based vs image-based, and what you'd pick for your own plant.
